answer.rationale: The incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle, foreclosing negotiate_terms, and the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so renewing as-is would fail the finance-mandated 18% cost cut. Memory c2 indicates a prior low-cost vendor switch achieved sharp cost reduction with quick, clean onboarding, which directly supports the cost objective. However, c6 (multi-year incumbent commitments cutting cost) potentially conflicts with the premise that the incumbent won't move on price, so it needs verification to confirm it doesn't offer a lower-risk path to the same savings. Given the line is at 94% committed volume with zero buffer, switching primary vendor carries real delivery-risk exposure during transition even if c2 holds, so I'm scoping this as a standard (not broad) rollout with contingency monitoring rather than an immediate full cutover, and flagging the risk rather than treating c2's past onboarding ease as guaranteed to repeat under tighter current constraints.
